approach: Write docs/spec.toml by hand from BRIEF.md "Project Olympus" sections 1 to 6 (line 550 to 864). It holds [[requirement]] tables (id, statement, kind, status, optional supersedes, one or more [[requirement.source]] with heading and verbatim quote) and optional [[open_question]] tables (id, question, two or more sides, each with heading and quote). Write xtask/tests/spec.rs with serde structs, a pure `check(spec, brief) -> Vec<String>` function, a whitespace-collapse helper, and a section splitter. It splits the Olympus part of BRIEF.md (from the line `# Project Olympus` to the line `## 7.`) at every heading line into (heading text, collapsed body). A quote passes only if it is a substring of the collapsed body of the section whose heading text equals the stated heading. This fixes the earlier job's gap, where a quote was checked against the whole brief. The tests are: the real spec passes, one in-memory negative per rule (non-verbatim quote, real quote under the wrong heading, duplicate id, dangling supersedes, no source, plus a quote in an open question), and a coverage test for R1 to R8 and sections 1 to 5. Then record the decision, the enforcement row and the changelog entry.

decisions.choice: Check each quote against the body of its stated heading, where a body runs from a heading line to the next heading line of any level, after whitespace collapse.
decisions.reason: Criterion 6 requires the quote to sit under its stated heading. Splitting at every heading keeps the rule simple, and the section headings in lines 560 to 864 are unique, so a heading maps to exactly one body.

rejected.option: Check against the whole of BRIEF.md
rejected.why: This was the earlier job's gap: a real quote under a wrong heading passed.

rejected.option: A body runs to the next heading of the same or higher level
rejected.why: A ## 3 quote would then pass when stated under ## 3 but come from 3.1. The stricter rule makes the producer name the exact subsection.

decisions.choice: Store the heading as plain text without the # marks (for example `R1 — Causal investigation`, `3.1 Preserve the original signal`) and match it to the heading line with the marks stripped.
decisions.reason: A stranger can read it, and the match is exact on text the brief contains.

rejected.why: It breaks when BRIEF.md moves; BRIEF.md is protected but is appended to.

decisions.choice: Quote fragments, not whole paragraphs, where a line would trip the boundary scan in xtask/tests/policy.rs. The Hermes row of the pantheon table contains the whole word `handoffs` (BRIEF.md line 597), which the scan bans in any tracked file but BRIEF.md, records/ and LICENSE. Quote the row only up to `context,` and keep the word out of every statement.
decisions.reason: A quote only has to be a substring, so truncating keeps it verbatim and keeps policy.rs passing (criterion 4). I read lines 550 to 864 and found no other banned whole word; `Release and operational checks` does not match, because the scan matches whole words.

rejected.why: policy.rs is a governance file and not a deliverable.

decisions.choice: Open questions are a separate [[open_question]] table with two or more quoted sides, each side checked by the same quote and heading rule, and with no field that resolves it.
decisions.reason: The request says to record a conflict or open choice quoting both sides and never resolve it. The producer adds one only where Sri's words really conflict or leave a choice open; no conflict is known to me from reading sections 1 to 6, so an empty list is acceptable and the schema and checker still support it.

rejected.why: A requirement is a single stated claim; the question has no statement to make.

decisions.choice: Keep the format as TOML read with the existing dev-dependencies `toml` 0.9 and `serde` (derive); do not change xtask/Cargo.toml unless a build needs it.
decisions.reason: The workspace already provides both (Cargo.toml lines 44 and 51) and xtask lists them under dev-dependencies, so the Rust-only default holds and nothing new is added.

rejected.why: JSON has no comments or multi-line strings, so quotes would be hard to read; YAML adds a dependency and its parsing surprises.
A checker would have to parse prose.

decisions.choice: Add one row to docs/enforcement.md (next free id M33) naming the new tests, and one entry in docs/decisions.md as D114 with the format, the choice of TOML, alternatives, a tradeoff, a reversal cost, and a note that sections 7 to 10, the governing philosophy and the 2026-10-17 addenda follow in a second job. Add a CHANGELOG.md line under [Unreleased].
decisions.reason: policy.rs M24 requires every backticked test name in enforcement.md to exist as a fn, so the row must use the exact test names. The decisions file uses a Case/Decision/Alternatives/Tradeoff/Reversal cost/Provenance layout (D113).

rejected.why: Verbatim sourcing would be enforced by a test not listed in the map, which breaks the 'mechanism' default.

files.purpose: The first layer of the cohesive spec: sourced requirements and open questions for Olympus sections 1 to 6, with the format described in a short header comment.
Parses the spec, checks quotes under their headings, ids, supersedes, sources and coverage, with in-memory negative cases.
Add D114: the spec format, TOML and alternatives, and the note that a second job covers sections 7 to 10, the governing philosophy and the addenda.
Add row M33 for verbatim sourcing, naming the blocking and allowing tests.
Record the new spec and its test under [Unreleased].
Expected to need no edit, since toml, serde and regex are already dev-dependencies; touch it only if the build shows a missing feature.

steps: Read BRIEF.md lines 550 to 864 once more and list one or more requirements per section: 1 Vision, 2 Pantheon, 3 plus 3.1 to 3.3, 4 plus Stages A to F, 5 plus Loop A, Loop B and 5.1, and R1 to R8. Merge repeats (for example roles by measured value in section 2 and R8; independent evaluation in Stage E and R4; root cause not assumed in 3.2 and Stage C).

Write docs/spec.toml with a header comment on the format (not mentioning who runs Athena or where), then [[requirement]] tables with ids such as `vision-1`, `r1-1`, kind, status `active`, an optional `supersedes`, and [[requirement.source]] tables of heading and quote; add [[open_question]] tables only for a real conflict or open choice, quoting both sides without resolving it. Check the quotes avoid banned whole words (notably `handoffs` in the Hermes row).

Write xtask/tests/spec.rs: root() from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR as in policy.rs; serde structs with deny_unknown_fields and enums for kind and status; `collapse(&str)`; `sections(brief)` returning heading to collapsed body for the Olympus part; `check(&Spec, &str) -> Vec<String>` covering quote under heading, unknown heading, duplicate id, dangling supersedes, no source, empty quote, open question sides; and `coverage(&Spec) -> Vec<String>` for R1 to R8 and sections 1 to 5, matching requirement sources' headings by their number prefix (`R1 `, `1.`, `3.1 ` count for 3, `Stage` and `Loop` counted for 4 and 5).

Add the tests: the real spec passes, one negative per rule built in memory by editing a clone of the parsed spec, the wrong-heading case, the subsection-under-parent case, the whitespace case, the open-question side case, and the coverage negative. Do not write the banned words in the file, since policy.rs scans it.
Add D114 to docs/decisions.md in the D113 layout, the M33 row to docs/enforcement.md, and a line to CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased].
Run `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo test -p xtask --test spec`, `cargo test -p xtask`, and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` once each, and fix findings.

risks.risk: The Hermes row (BRIEF.md line 597) holds `handoffs`, which policy.rs bans in tracked files, so a full-row quote fails criterion 4.
risks.mitigation: Quote fragments that avoid the word, keep it out of statements, and run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` before finishing.

risks.risk: Special characters in quotes (em dash, arrows, straight quotes, table pipes) make a hand-typed quote differ from the brief.
risks.mitigation: Prefer single-line quotes, use TOML literal strings (''' ''') or escapes, and let the whitespace-collapse test catch mismatch. Check against the brief text as read, with dashes (— in headings) copied exactly.

risks.risk: policy.rs M24 fails if the enforcement row names a test that does not exist.
risks.mitigation: Name the spec's own test functions exactly as in the M33 row, and run the policy test.

risks.risk: The same headings could also occur in earlier text, and a loose search would pick the wrong section.
risks.mitigation: The splitter starts at the line `# Project Olympus` and stops at `## 7.`, and a test asserts all headings used by the spec are found there, once each.

risks.risk: The known failing athena-data test makes the full `cargo test --locked` red regardless of this change.
risks.mitigation: Do not touch athena-data; the failing digest test is out of scope. Run only xtask tests plus clippy and fmt.

demonstrations.method: The test `the_real_spec_passes` parses docs/spec.toml, and `every_requirement_has_the_required_fields` and the coverage test run on it. Open docs/spec.toml and read that each requirement has id, statement, kind, status and sources with heading and quote.
demonstrations.observes: The tests pass. Kind is one of goal, requirement, constraint or acceptance and status is active or superseded (the serde enums reject others). Every R1 to R8 and sections 1 to 5 has at least one requirement.

demonstrations.method: Content check by reading docs/spec.toml, plus the test `open_question_sides_are_checked_like_sources`, which feeds a question with a non-verbatim side and expects a failure. Read that a duplicate statement (for example the independent-evaluation idea in Stage E and R4, or the roles-measured-by-value idea in section 2 and R8) is one requirement with several sources.
demonstrations.observes: No requirement repeats another's claim, merged ones list several sources, and any open question quotes both sides and holds no resolution field.

demonstrations.method: Read the new D114 entry in the diff.
demonstrations.observes: It names the spec format, TOML, the alternatives (YAML, JSON, Markdown), and says sections 7 to 10, the governing philosophy and the 2026-10-17 addenda follow in a second job.

demonstrations.method: Run the policy test, then `git status` to see the changed files.
demonstrations.observes: Policy tests pass, and the changed files are only docs/spec.toml, xtask/tests/spec.rs, docs/decisions.md, docs/enforcement.md and CHANGELOG.md, with no athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflow or lint file.
demonstrations.fails_without: Quoting the Hermes row in full or writing a banned word in a statement or in the test source would make `athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where` fail on docs/spec.toml or xtask/tests/spec.rs.

demonstrations.method: Run the test file. The negative tests mutate a copy of the parsed real spec in memory (change one quote, repeat an id, set supersedes to an unknown id, empty the sources, drop the requirements for R3 or section 2) and assert `check` returns the matching message. A whitespace test shows a quote with different line breaks still passes.
demonstrations.observes: The real spec gives no errors and each mutated spec gives the specific error.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the checker did not compare quotes, ids, supersedes targets and sources, the negative tests `a_quote_that_is_not_in_the_brief_fails`, `a_duplicate_id_fails`, `a_dangling_supersedes_fails` and `a_requirement_without_a_source_fails` would see no error and fail their assertions. If coverage were not checked, `a_missing_requirement_for_a_section_or_r_fails` would fail.

demonstrations.method: Run the whole xtask suite. The test `a_real_quote_under_the_wrong_heading_fails` takes a real source from the spec and pairs it with another real heading (for example R1 quote under R2), plus a quote from a subsection stated under its parent section.
demonstrations.observes: The checker returns a heading error for each, and the real spec still passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the checker searched the whole brief, `a_real_quote_under_the_wrong_heading_fails` would pass the bad spec and its assertion that an error is returned would fail.

demonstrations.method: Run clippy, `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`.
demonstrations.observes: All three exit clean, including the M24 check that the enforcement row's test names exist as fns in xtask/tests/spec.rs.

open_questions: xtask/Cargo.toml is a listed deliverable but toml, serde and regex are already there; I judge no change is needed.
I found no real conflict or open choice in sections 1 to 6; the producer must reread the text and may end with no [[open_question]] entries. If so, the spec header should say so.
The next free ids are M33 in docs/enforcement.md and D114 in docs/decisions.md as of the base snapshot (M32 and D113 are the last I saw).
